name: content-strategy
description: Decide what content to make, fix or retire: a fate table for existing pages with the rule behind each decision, a topic map with buyer stage, intent and the new information each topic needs, a plan sized to the team's real hours with a printed planning score, writer briefs with proof slots, and lead-magnet plans. It plans; it does not write the content or build campaigns.

interface.longDescription: Five connected skills for teams with limited hours. Decide the fate of existing pages (keep, update, merge, redirect, retire or leave alone) with a numbered rule on every row and a list of what could not be checked. Build a topic map where every topic names the new information behind it or is marked commodity. Turn a list of ideas into a plan sized exactly to the team's hours, with a printed planning score and a not-now list. Write briefs a writer can work from, with proof slots instead of invented data, and plan lead magnets with an honest gate decision. Dates alone never decide a page's fate. It plans; it does not write the content.
defaultPrompt: Keep, update, merge or cut: /blog/ap-tips-2021 (40 visits), /blog/ap-automation-guide (2,100), /blog/ap-tips-2023 (35).
Demo goal, 1 writer 6h/wk. Topics: ROI guide (own data), customer story (own data), AP glossary (none). What fits this quarter?
Topic map for Northwind Ledger: AP automation for 50-500 staff firms, goal demo requests, we have 40 customer interviews.
